summary.en: Preserve precedence and associativity while moving operators into postfix and prefix order.
summary.bn: Operator-এর অগ্রাধিকার ও বাঁধার দিক ঠিক রেখে postfix ও prefix বানাও।

notes: Programs use C17 with explicit bounds and ownership checks.

examples.title: Convert infix with an operator stack
examples.explanationHtml: Multiplication leaves the operator stack before addition, producing ABC*+.

examples.title: Keep exponentiation right associative
examples.explanationHtml: Equal ^ operators stay stacked, producing ABC^^ for A^(B^C).

examples.title: Build prefix from completed postfix subexpressions
examples.explanationHtml: AB-C* combines into *-ABC; the left and right operands retain their roles.

examples.title: Reject a missing operand
examples.explanationHtml: The scan finishes while need_operand is true, so it rejects incomplete syntax.

practice.title: Convert uppercase infix
practice.statementHtml: Read one line of at most 24 characters using A..Z, spaces, binary + - * / ^ and parentheses. Print the prompt then Postfix: and the converted text, or Invalid. Unary operators and adjacent operands are not allowed.
hints: Pop equal precedence for left-associative operators only.

practice.title: Produce prefix notation
practice.statementHtml: Use the same infix input restrictions and prompt. Print Prefix: followed by the expression, or Invalid.
hints: Combine the right postfix fragment after the left fragment.

practice.title: Count operators in a validated infix expression
practice.statementHtml: Use the infix converter input grammar and prompt. Print Operators: and the binary-operator count after a valid conversion, or Invalid.
hints: Count operators in the completed postfix output, not grouping markers.

practice.title: Produce both unambiguous expression forms
practice.statementHtml: Use the converter grammar and prompt. Print Postfix: and Prefix: on separate lines for valid input; otherwise print Invalid.
hints: Build prefix from ordered left and right postfix fragments.

quiz.prompt: For A-B-C, which operation groups first?
When incoming ^ meets top ^, what does this converter do?
quiz.explanation: Keeping equal exponentiation operators delays the left one.
Multiplication binds B and C before addition.

quiz.prompt: Where does an opening parenthesis go during conversion?
quiz.explanation: It forms a boundary for later popping.
The multiplication root comes before its left subtraction subtree.

quiz.prompt: Why is the shunting-yard operator work linear?
options: The stack always has one item
Each operator is pushed and popped at most once
quiz.explanation: Nested loops still perform only a linear number of stack operations.

quiz.prompt: Does ^ mean exponentiation in C17 itself?
options: No; C uses ^ for bitwise XOR
quiz.explanation: The converter defines an expression grammar; it does not evaluate C operators.

quiz.prompt: How many operators remain after pushing + then *?
quiz.explanation: Both operators wait, with multiplication at the top.

quiz.prompt: What does the precedence comparison between * and + print?
quiz.explanation: Multiplication has the greater precedence rank.

quiz.prompt: Which operand fragment is popped first from postfix AB-?
quiz.explanation: The right fragment is on top and must be kept on the right.

quiz.prompt: Why must A(B) be rejected by the stated grammar?
quiz.explanation: The operand is followed by a group without an explicit binary operator.
The parenthesized left exponentiation completes before the outer exponentiation.

keyPoints.en: An operator stack delays operations until their operands are ready.
keyPoints.bn: Operand প্রস্তুত হওয়া পর্যন্ত operator স্ট্যাকে থাকে।

keyPoints.en: Equal left-associative operators are popped before the incoming operator.
keyPoints.bn: বাম থেকে বাঁধা operator-এর অগ্রাধিকার সমান হলে আগেরটি বের করো।

keyPoints.en: Exponentiation is right associative in this expression grammar.
keyPoints.bn: এখানকার grammar-এ ঘাত ডান দিক থেকে বাঁধে।

keyPoints.en: Parentheses group operands but never appear in postfix output.
keyPoints.bn: বন্ধনী operand-এর দল ঠিক করে, postfix-এ থাকে না।

keyPoints.en: Prefix construction preserves ordered left and right subexpressions.
keyPoints.bn: Prefix বানানোর সময় বাম ও ডান অংশের ক্রম ঠিক রাখো।

examQuestions.question: Convert A/(B-C)+D to postfix and prefix.
examQuestions.answerHtml: The grouped subtraction is BC-. Division gives ABC-/. Addition gives ABC-/D+. Prefix is +/A-BCD, whose root is addition and left child is division.

examQuestions.question: Show the operator stack and output after each token of A*(B+C)-D.
Derive postfix and prefix for A^B^C and explain why reversing text alone is unsafe.
examQuestions.answerHtml: Parse the expression as A^(B^C). Its postfix is ABC^^ and its prefix is ^A^BC. Reversing the text changes token order but does not preserve associativity automatically. Building ordered subexpressions from postfix keeps each left and right child in place.
